artists.biography: James is a British rock band from Manchester, England. They formed in 1982 and were active throughout the 1980s, but most successful during the 1990s. Their hit singles include "Come Home", "Sit Down", and "She's a Star" as well as their American college radio hit "Laid". Following the departure of lead singer Tim Booth in 2001, the band became inactive but re-formed in January 2007, returning for a new album and international tour. Up to 2010, the band had sold more than 25 million albums worldwide.

perplexity.description:
All The Colours Of You, released in June 2021, is the 16th studio album by the English rock band James. Produced by Grammy-winning producer Jacknife Lee at his Topanga Canyon studio, the album marks a stylistic evolution for the band, blending electronic textures with their signature rock sound. The collaboration was conducted remotely, with frontman Tim Booth working from Los Angeles and the rest of the band based in the UK. The result is an album that features choral harmonies, progressive rock elements, and a surge of surrealist electro-synth, particularly evident in tracks like "Zero" and the title track "All The Colours Of You." Lyrically, the album addresses themes of global politics, climate change, and the pandemic, reflecting the turbulent times in which it was created.

Musically, All The Colours Of You stands out in James’ extensive discography for its experimental approach and modern production. It was the band’s first release on Virgin Music Label & Artist Services and their first under new publishing arrangements with Kobalt Music. The album received positive critical attention for its ambitious sound and emotional depth, with reviewers noting its fresh direction while maintaining the band’s core identity. Singles such as "All The Colours Of You," "Beautiful Beaches," "Recover," and "Isabella" helped drive its reception, and the album was supported by a series of live performances and tours, further cementing its place as a significant entry in James’ catalog.
